title: st.date_input dropdown showing the wrong year in constrained range
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary When selecting a date from the dropdown with a range defined that crosses the boundary between two years, the year is pinned to the earlier of the two even when looking at months in the later. If a date is selected, it renders correctly in the input box but the dropdown continues to be wrong. I used uv to install streamlit 1.62.0. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python #In main.py: from datetime import datetime import streamlit as st a = st.date_input("Input:", min_value=datetime(2024,8,3), max_value=datetime(2025,2,3), value=None) st.write(a) #---------------------------------------------------- #In pyproject.toml: [project] name = "streamlit-bug" version = "0.1.0" requires-python = ">=3.13" dependencies = [ "streamlit>=1.62.0", ] ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Create directory containing main.py and pyproject.toml as given in the code example. 2. Run `uv sync` to set up environment 3. Run the app with `uv run streamlit run main.py` 4. On the app page, select the date input. ### Expected Behavior The date input dropdown should open in February, 2025. When the 1st of February is selected, the input should display 2025/02/01. If the year in the dropdown menu is selected, it should display a list of 2024 and 2025. ### Current Behavior The date dropdown opens in February, 2025 but displays it as February, 2024. When the 1st of February is selected, the input displays 2025/02/01. If the year in the dropdown menu is selected, it displays a list of only 2024. ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.62.0 - Python version: 3.13.14 - Operating System: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (running in WSL) - Browser: Google Chrome ### Additional Information _No response_

comments.body:
**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-16686)

This is a frontend bug in the `st.date_input` calendar header: when `min_value`/`max_value` span a year boundary and the max date’s month/day is earlier than the min date’s (here `2024-08-03` → `2025-02-03`), the popover grid is on February 2025 but the header shows **February 2024**, and the year dropdown lists only **2024**. Selecting a day still commits the correct 2025 date, so the value path is fine; only the month/year picker UI is wrong. The same header is shared with `st.datetime_input`.

Likely cause: React Aria’s `CalendarYearPicker` (`useCalendarYearPicker`, `react-aria-components` 1.20.0) builds year options by starting at `minValue` and adding one year at a time until the date exceeds `maxValue`. `2024-08-03 + 1 year` is `2025-08-03`, which is after `2025-02-03`, so 2025 is never added. Streamlit then renders the year trigger from that item list (`CalendarPopoverHeader`), so it stays on the only remaining year (2024) even while the calendar grid shows February 2025. There is already a local workaround in `CalendarPopoverHeader` for a related RAC year-picker bug (stale month on controlled `focusedValue`), but it does not fix year-list generation. A secondary Streamlit issue: `getInitialFocusedDate` clamps to `minDate` but not `maxDate`, so with `value=None` and today after the max, the focused date starts out of range.

### Related Issues

- [#9667](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9667) — Same class of year-dropdown failure when the allowed range crosses a year boundary (years missing/disabled). Filed against the old Baseweb picker and closed after the RAC migration; this issue is the RAC equivalent, not a duplicate.
- [#9922](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9922) — Year options were treated as unavailable unless the *currently displayed month* was valid in that year. Same underlying “year list does not mean any date in that year is selectable” problem; also Baseweb-era and closed.
- [#14799](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14799) — Duplicate of #9667 with a side-by-side repro of inconsistent year enabling at range edges. Useful for expected vs actual year-picker behavior; closed as duplicate/upstream.
